project: (note) Edits to code may be reverted/commented out by others; always verify changes are present and compile before proceeding.

FINDINGS (ordered by severity)

1. BLOCKING — flutter_app/lib/network/network_session_manager.dart:65,421,426
One shared `_sessionToken` field for ALL networks. `_startSession` does `_sessionToken = result.sessionToken;` and hands every FaNetworkWs the same closure `sessionToken: () => _sessionToken ?? ''`. Joining a second network overwrites the token the FIRST network's live socket will use on its next reconnect → the first network's realtime link 401s in a permanent reconnect loop (its session token is network-scoped per the join contract), and `sendText` keeps "sending" into a dead socket. `createNetwork`/`createChannel` (lines ~379/392) also pin `_sessionToken` (last joined network) onto fresh clients. Multi-network membership is a first-class feature here (wallet.networks + sessions are both maps, sidebar lists all memberships), so this breaks it deterministically.
Fix: keep the token per session — pass the JoinResult's sessionToken into FaNetworkWs as a captured value (read once per connect via the existing closure, but bound at construction) or maintain `Map<networkId,String>`.

2. IMPORTANT — browser_ext/dart/src/dap/dap_client.dart:256 (+ dap_integration.dart:188-196)
`DapClient._connect()` calls `new _WebSocket(wsUrl)` (line 256) with NO try/catch around the sync constructor. `wsUrl` carries `dap_token` and/or `token` secrets (lines 244-247). For a malformed credentialed URL the browser throws SyntaxError whose message echoes the FULL URL including the secret ("Failed to construct 'WebSocket': The URL 'wss://…?dap_token=…' is invalid."). The throw propagates through `client.start()` (line 187) into `DapIntegration.start()`'s catch-all, which prints the raw exception: `print('[fa] dap identity/start failed: $e')` (line 191) and also stores `'error': '$e'` in the status map that reaches the panel. This violates the file's own contract ("diagnostics must stay secret-free"; cf. the careful close-reason sanitising a few lines below, and WebHubTransport._connect in the app which exists precisely to sanitize this). 
Fix: wrap the constructor in try/catch inside `_connect` and rethrow a constant `StateError('hub WebSocket connection failed')` (mirroring agent_network_transport_web.dart); never print raw `$e` from this path.

3. IMPORTANT — flutter_app/lib/services/agent_network_controller.dart:214-241
Concurrent-join race: `_join` guards with `if (… || _hub != null) return;` BEFORE the first `await` (`_loadIdentity`, line 225), but `_hub` is assigned only after that await (line 239). If `setEnabled(true)`, `saveConnection`, or `joinEnrollment` runs while the boot-time `start()→_joinSaved()→_join()` is still awaiting identity load, BOTH calls pass the guard → two live HubMessagingRepository instances, two sockets for the same agent (the hub evicts one), the first repository is never stopped (leaked reconnect loop), `_linkSub` is overwritten (leaked subscription), and the fabric is swapped twice.
Fix: serialize joins with a future chain (`_joinChain = _joinChain.then((_) => _join(...))`) or set a `_joining` flag before the first await.

4. SUGGESTION — flutter_app/lib/network/fa_network_client.dart:740,678-683
`_errorFor` falls back to `var message = response.body;` — the ENTIRE raw, non-JSON error body becomes the exception message, and `_request` then interpolates it into AppLog (lines 678-683). A 502 HTML page (or any multi-KB body, or a body with embedded newlines) lands verbatim in the app log: log bloat + log-line/format injection. Fix: truncate to ~200 chars on a single line in `_errorFor` (or at the log call).

5. SUGGESTION — lib/src/messaging/io_hub_transport.dart:81-84 and 109-114
`loadHubIdentity` writes the temp key file with the process umask (typically 0644), renames it into place, and only THEN chmods 0600 — a window where the Ed25519/X25519 private scalars are world-readable on multi-user systems; on chmod failure it only prints a stderr warning. The twin `saveHubIdentity` writes the key file directly (non-atomic, default perms until chmod) even though the file's own comment says a torn direct write breaks later loads. Fix: chmod the temp before rename, and route saveHubIdentity through the same temp+rename+chmod flow.
